newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Skoda buys Brown and Root BRSK stake.
newsitem.headline: Czech Skoda buys Brown and Root BRSK stake.

text.p: Czech engineering concern Skoda a.s. on Friday said it had bought the 66 percent stake owned by British firm Brown and Root in the two firms' joint venture, Brown and Root Skoda (BRSK).
Skoda, which now owns 100 percent of the venture, added in a statement that it had decided to more than double BRSK's basic capital to 377 million crowns ($13.3 million) from 176 million.
The two firms established BRSK in 1993.

BRSK, which will now revert back to its original name, Skoda DIZ sro, will work in "engineering activities for the Energo Skoda Plzen division, and further in the areas of heavy machinery, chemical, foodstuffs and paper industries, and in ecological construction", the statement added.
For 1995, Skoda posted a consolidated loss of 432 million crowns on sales of 21 billion.
-- Alan Crosby, Prague Newsroom, 42-2-2423-0003 ($ = 28.37 Czech Crowns)
